$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. ExecutionReceipt per FB-RAT-EXE-001. Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<ExecutionReceipt> (see schemas/common/envelope.schema.json). `receiptId` is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID. Receipts are append-only (FB-RAT-COM-006) — a corrected receipt is a NEW receipt referencing the old one via `unknownFields`/provenance, never an in-place edit.
title: ExecutionReceipt
description: The durable, terminal record of one ExecutionRequest run: a target snapshot, the revision actually executed, a capsule digest, timings, exit state, logs, resource usage, output ArtifactRefs (reused from schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json, not redefined), recorded side effects, and result verification — kept structurally separate from success (FB-RAT-EXE-009). Emitted once, at (or after) a terminal ExecutionHandle.state.

receiptId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this receipt (FB-RAT-COM-002).

requestId.description: References the ExecutionRequest.id this receipt reports on.

handleId.description: References the ExecutionHandle.handleId whose terminal state this receipt is derived from.

id.description: The ExecutionTarget.id this ran on — a stable reference, but the rest of this object is a POINT-IN-TIME COPY of that target's fields at execution time, not a live reference, because a target's own trust/fingerprint/arch can legitimately change later without rewriting history.

targetSnapshot.description: Duplicated subset of schemas/execution/target.schema.json's ExecutionTarget fields per this repo's convention of duplicating small shared sub-shapes across schema files (docs/ratified/COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md §5) rather than reaching into another document's $defs.

revision.description: The exact revision that actually executed (resolved, e.g. a full git commit SHA rather than a branch name — FB-RAT-STR-004 revision visibility). Null only when the corresponding ExecutionRequest.workingRevision was also null (no git-scoped working tree).

capsuleDigest.description: Digest+length over the serialized 'execution capsule' — the exact command, args, resolved env, and secret-handle references (never secret values) that were sent to the provider (FB-RAT-COM-005). Lets a caller later prove exactly what was requested to run, independent of the human-readable `operation.command` string on the originating ExecutionRequest.

startedAtUtc.description: Null only if the operation never left QUEUED (e.g. cancelled before PREPARING).

durationMs.description: finishedAtUtc - startedAtUtc in milliseconds, when startedAtUtc is non-null. Null when startedAtUtc is null.

terminationCause.description: Android 12+ phantom-process-killer awareness (platform grounding): required non-null when `exitState` is TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN (see the if/then below) — a receipt MUST record that the process may simply have been SIGKILLed with no chance to report, not silently omit the cause.

ref.description: Full log bundle as an ArtifactRef (reused from schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json, not redefined), or null if no durable log bundle was produced.

excerpt.description: Short inline excerpt (e.g. the log tail) for quick display without fetching `ref`. MUST be redaction-scanned before population, identically to schemas/common/error.schema.json's ErrorEnvelope.detail (binding rule: API keys are never logged) — see fixtures/execution/adversarial/receipt-secret-leak-in-log-excerpt.adversarial.json for the fixture this guards against, and fixtures/execution/valid/receipt-log-excerpt-redacted-clean.json for the compliant counterpart.

redactionApplied.description: Producer's own claim that credential-shaped substrings were scanned and redacted from `excerpt` (and from whatever `ref` points at) before this receipt was written. A schema cannot verify the claim is true — see the adversarial fixture referenced above, where this field is (incorrectly) true while `excerpt` still contains a live-looking secret, which is exactly the case a real implementation's redaction step MUST prevent from ever being constructible.

thermalStateObserved.description: FB-RAT-EXE-006 P0-normative half: thermal STATE OBSERVABILITY. Null only when the target/provider does not support thermal observability at all (see ExecutionRequest.budget.thermalStateObservabilityRequired); UNKNOWN means observability was attempted but inconclusive, distinct from never having attempted it (null).

resourceSummary.description: All fields nullable/optional — not every provider (e.g. a CI_PIPELINE target) can report every resource dimension a LOCAL_ANDROID target can.

outputs.description: Realized output artifacts, reused as-is from schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json (not redefined here) — each entry's own `producerReceipt.receiptObjectId` SHOULD point back at this receipt's ContractEnvelope.objectId.

external.description: True if this side effect is visible/persists outside the immediate execution session (a git push, a device flash, a dispatched CI run) — FALSE for effects fully contained and already reversed within this same execution (e.g. a temp file cleaned up before exit).

sideEffects.description: Real-world side effects this execution is known (or believed) to have caused. Required non-empty when `exitState` is FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE (see the if/then below) — a receipt MUST NOT use that exit state and then leave this array empty, since the whole point of the state is to name what may have happened.

state.description: FB-RAT-EXE-009: operation success and result verification are separate states. See the if/then rules below tying this to `exitState`.

method.description: How verification was performed, e.g. 'checksum compare against expected artifact', 'STK500 flash-verify readback', 'exit code + test-report parse'.

sourceLocation.description: FB-RAT-COM-008 — where the executed operation came from (repo path, device path, workflow file ref).

projectRevision.description: FB-RAT-COM-008 — project/repo revision in effect (often equal to `revision` above, but named separately because the two can differ, e.g. a device-flash operation whose 'project' is the firmware repo while `revision` is the flashed image's own version string).

initiatingPrincipal.description: FB-RAT-COM-008 — who or what initiated this execution (user id, agent name, scheduled-loop id).

evidenceLinks.description: FB-RAT-COM-008 — optional supporting evidence links (logs, related receipts, screenshots).

provenance.description: FB-RAT-COM-008 provenance minimum, duplicated inline per this repo's convention (mirrors ArtifactRef.ProducerReceiptRef in schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json's $defs) rather than cross-file $ref'd into another document's $defs.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

allOf.$comment: FB-RAT-EXE-009: exitState SUCCEEDED requires verification.state VERIFIED — a plain success without verification MUST use SUCCEEDED_UNVERIFIED instead.
FB-RAT-EXE-009: SUCCEEDED_UNVERIFIED MUST NOT claim verification.state VERIFIED or FAILED — either it wasn't attempted, or it was explicitly skipped.
FB-RAT-EXE-009: a failed exitState MUST NOT simultaneously claim verification.state VERIFIED.
Platform grounding: a TARGET_STATE_UNKNOWN receipt MUST record a terminationCause (SIGKILL suspected, reconnect uncertainty, etc.) rather than leaving the reason implicit.
A receipt MUST NOT declare FAILED_SIDE_EFFECTS_POSSIBLE and then leave sideEffects empty — name what may have happened.

ExecutionExitState.description: The terminal subset of schemas/execution/handle.schema.json's ExecutionState enum — a receipt is only ever emitted once a handle has reached one of these six terminal states.

TerminationCause.description: NORMAL: the operation ran to its own natural conclusion. USER_CANCELLED: an explicit cancel() completed. SIGKILL_SUSPECTED: heartbeat/process evidence points at an Android 12+ phantom-process-kill or similar OS-level kill. PROCESS_DEATH_UNSPECIFIED: the owning process is confirmed gone but the specific cause is not known. RECONNECT_UNKNOWN: a reconnect() attempt could not establish state (FB-RAT-EXE-004) — see schemas/execution/handle.schema.json's ReconnectAttempt.outcome for the finer-grained reason.

algorithm.description: Digest algorithm; SHA-256 or stronger only (FB-RAT-COM-005).

IntegrityRef.description: Duplicated from schemas/common/envelope.schema.json's $defs/IntegrityRef per this repo's convention (docs/ratified/COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md §5) of duplicating small shared sub-shapes rather than cross-file $ref into another document's $defs.
